title: Thickness Optimization of SiO2/TiO2 Bilayer on Glass
scientific_hypothesis: A planar bilayer stack with low-index SiO2 as the incident-facing layer and high-index TiO2 as the substrate-facing layer, with optimized thicknesses between 40-160 nm, yields a lower arithmetic mean reflectance across 450-700 nm than the reverse ordering or unoptimized quarter-wave stacks.
design_principle: Antireflection in a two-layer system relies on destructive interference between reflections at the air-coating, coating-coating, and coating-substrate interfaces. Placing the lower index material (SiO2, n=1.46) next to air (n=1.0) provides a smoother impedance transition than placing high-index TiO2 (n=2.40) directly against air, which typically reduces the peak reflectance amplitude before interference effects are tuned by thickness.
proposed_topology: Air (n=1.0) / SiO2 (variable thickness) / TiO2 (variable thickness) / Glass Substrate (n=1.52)
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thickness must remain within 40 nm to 160 nm to satisfy process constraints
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for normal incidence s-polarization
Fresnel reflection coefficients at planar interfaces
expected_advantages: Concentrating the evaluation budget (64 samples) on a single topology allows finer sampling of the thickness landscape compared to splitting the budget between two orderings.
SiO2-first topology aligns with standard broadband AR design heuristics for glass substrates.
known_risks: The global minimum might exist in the reverse (TiO2/SiO2) ordering, which this route would identify only as a local failure, requiring a second round to investigate.
Constant index assumption may deviate from real dispersion, though the problem statement mandates it.
execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method optimization for a planar three-medium stack: Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 (SiO2 (Gao), n=1.46, lossless), Layer 2 (TiO2 (Siefke), n=2.40, lossless), Substrate (Glass, n=1.52, lossless). The stack order is fixed as Air/SiO2 (Gao)/TiO2 (Siefke)/Glass. Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2 independently, with both constrained to the range [40, 160] nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees) over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm, sampled at 5 nm intervals. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Perform up to 64 solver evaluations. Report the best candidate's thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance.
